title: Urban Appraisal: Physiological Recording during Rating of Different Urban Environments
description: This dataset contains continuous EEG, ECG and electrodermal activity (EDA) recordings from 63 participants who viewed and rated Streetview images of different urban environments on a desktop PC. It was collected to investigate how urban environments and their elements influence urban appraisals and neural responses, including stimulus-onset ERPs (P1, N1, P3, LPP). Each participant rated 56 images on nine subjective scales, and semantic segmentation of the images provides predictors for subjective and neural responses.
methods_description: 64-channel wet-electrode EEG (10-20 system, FCz reference) was recorded together with ECG (right clavicle and left shinbone) and EDA (middle and ring fingers of the non-dominant hand). A BrainAmp DC amplifier from BrainProducts was used at 500 Hz, 16-bit resolution, with a 0.016 Hz high-pass filter. Stimuli were presented with Psychtoolbox in MATLAB on a 27-inch monitor. Each of 56 images was rated on nine scales (504 trials) in two blocks separated by a break, with 3-minute eyes-open baselines at the start and end.
